properties.name: Skill use is triggered by the situation, not remembered — and the USER must never be the trigger
properties.statement:
An agent's use of reflow2's SKILLS must not decay over a session while its use of the TOOLS holds. Measured on reflow2's own repo, 2026-07-31, in a long session: `loop_status` was called unprompted throughout and every write went through `record_change`, two-sided checksum accepts and one-export-per-commit — but exactly two skills were loaded all session, and both only because the user typed a slash command. `impact-check`, `link-artifacts`, `capture-intent`, `revise-design`, `check-health` and `report-friction` were never loaded. THE THREE BL-74 RUNGS ARE ALL `verified` AND THIS STILL HAPPENED, which is the finding: they are working as designed and do not reach this.

THE STRUCTURAL REASON. The rungs compute LOOP DEBT — a property of graph state, which is what `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` correctly insists on. Skills fire on SITUATIONS: about to change code, just wrote a file, the user just shared an idea. The graph cannot see any of those, so the trigger mechanism covers one half of the problem and structurally cannot reach the other. That is why `impact-check` was dropped hardest — nothing in the system knows an edit is coming, and by the time the graph could tell, the edit has happened and the blast radius is a post-mortem rather than a check.

WHAT COST SOMETHING, honestly: `impact-check` was never run before changing `snapshot_node`, `delete_edge` and `delete_node`; the blast radius was reasoned about by hand instead of computed. `link-artifacts` was never loaded and a stale `art:nodes` checksum was nearly shipped — caught only by grepping after the export, which then required restoring the export and redoing it. `check-health` cost nothing, because `detect_defects` was run bare and did catch the island.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, in the order the evidence supports, NOT a decided design. (1) Extend the PostToolUse hook from COUNTING writes to matching SHAPES — a file edit with no ChangeEvent in the window means impact-check, an artifact checksum drift means link-artifacts. `req:nudge-covers-bypass` already arms the nudge on file-edit events and already names impact-check and link-artifacts, and is `verified`; what is missing is the shape-matching, not the trigger. (2) A refusal, where refusing is honest — reflow2's strongest mechanism, proven three times in this session alone — but only where skipping is genuinely wrong, because a guard that punishes correct work is the failure this project keeps naming.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS SESSION: BL-74 called this adoption-critical and found it in the author's own fleet, self-reported by the driving agent. This is the same failure observed from inside, on a session with MORE context about reflow2 than a consumer's agent will have — so it is likely a best case rather than a typical one.

=== ⭐ SECOND OBSERVATION, 2026-08-06 — SIX DAYS LATER, MECHANISM (1) SHIPPED AND VERIFIED, AND THE USER IS STILL THE TRIGGER ===

Anthony, unprompted, mid-session: "as always, please use reflow2 skills and tools to implement any of this. this always gives us a first use case to see where we need to fix/improve reflow2 skills and tools. I STILL DON'T LIKE REMINDING THIS ALL THE TIME (which needs to be an enduring requirement to increase the probability that an agent will use reflow2 skills and tools and not rely on itself)."

⭐ HIS WORDS PROMOTE THIS FROM AN OBSERVATION TO A STANDING OBLIGATION, AND THAT IS THE REVISION: the requirement was written as "skill use must not DECAY over a session". It is now stronger — THE USER MUST NOT BE THE REMINDER MECHANISM AT ALL. A design brain whose correct operation depends on its owner repeating an instruction has moved the burden onto the person it was built to relieve, and it will not survive contact with a consumer who does not know to say it.

WHAT MAKES THIS OBSERVATION DIFFERENT FROM THE FIRST, AND WORSE: `cap:skill-triggers` is now `verified` — the shape-matching hook of candidate mechanism (1) was BUILT and WORKS. It fired correctly in this very session (the Stop hook caught graph writes with no loop check, and was obeyed). The self-assessment for 2026-08-06 is genuinely better than 2026-07-31: capture-intent and brainstorm were both loaded and followed, and `claim_region`, `propagate_change`, `reconcile_artifacts`, `set_artifact_checksums`, `describe_schema`, `compose_and_analyse`, `pair_designs`, `detect_defects` and `loop_status` were all used unprompted. AND IT STILL WAS NOT ENOUGH — `list_skills` was never called at session start, `link-artifacts` was never loaded although its work was done by hand, and `revise-design` was loaded only after the user's reminder.

⭐ THE BLIND SPOT IS NOW NAMEABLE, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL. `cap:skill-triggers` recognises SHAPES IN THE GRAPH-WRITE STREAM — an edit with no ChangeEvent, a change never propagated, a capture with no gap pass. Every shape it knows is a shape that requires the agent to have ALREADY TOUCHED THE GRAPH. THE ONE SITUATION IT CANNOT SEE IS "NO SKILL HAS BEEN LOADED", because a skill load is not a graph write and nothing counts it. That is not a defect in the capability; it is the exact hole `req:skill-adherence-is-measured` was written to fill — AND THAT REQUIREMENT IS `deferred`. The DEPENDS_ON edge between them already says so in its own evidence: "without a measurement, whether that requirement is ever met is unknowable — the decay it names was found by asking an agent, not by any mechanism." Today it was found by asking an agent again. That is now twice.

⭐ THE NEW RATIONALE, WHICH RAISES THE PRIORITY AND WAS NOT IN THE FIRST VERSION: Anthony's reason is not process hygiene. It is INSTRUMENTATION — "this always gives us a first use case to see where we need to fix/improve reflow2 skills and tools." Every skill invocation is a test of that skill against real work, and this session proved the point twice over: following brainstorm surfaced that its step 2 is STALE (it instructs `set_decision_status` to `proposed` because "add_decision defaults to accepted", which stopped being true on 2026-07-25), and following capture-intent's "search before you add" is the only reason the flo2 capture did not mint duplicates of `req:many-designs-one-service`. AN AGENT THAT RECONSTRUCTS A SKILL FROM GENERAL COMPETENCE PRODUCES ROUGHLY THE RIGHT WORK AND GENERATES NO EVIDENCE. The skills are reflow2's product surface, and unexercised product surface is how [BL-176] hid for eleven releases.

SO SKIPPING A SKILL HAS TWO COSTS, NOT ONE: the work is done less well, AND the defect in the skill goes unfound. The second is the one that compounds.
